reader.requirement: At 85 USE AFTER STANDARD ERROR PROCEDURE and USE AFTER STANDARD EXCEPTION PROCEDURE must be accepted and bound identically for every operand form (file-name list, INPUT, OUTPUT, I-O, EXTEND), so that the two spellings select the same declarative and count as the same statement for SR3 (one file-name per USE) and SR6 (one USE per open mode).

edition-consulted.switches: below 2002 refuses Format 1 without AFTER or without PROCEDURE (COBOL0900) and Formats 3/4 (EXCEPTION CONDITION, EXCEPTION OBJECT); both ERROR and EXCEPTION spellings pass untouched
DialectLevel >= 2002 adds the SORT GR17 exit filter; 85 emits the plain try/finally body for every Format 1 declarative whatever its spelling

reader.edition-search: grep of Edition/DialectLevel in ProcedureTableBuilder.DeclBindUse (only ctx.Edition.Error/At reporting), the useStatement grammar alternative (EXCEPTION | ERROR) with no predicate, VisitUseStatement in VersionConformancePass, DialectLevel in DispatchEmitter/EcEmitter
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: the grammar's (EXCEPTION | ERROR) alternative and DeclBindUse never read which word was written, at any edition
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_bf27_05 shows each spelling on an explicit file-name; the mode operands and the synonymy's effect on SR3/SR6 duplicate checks are not exercised

probes.printed: D1-ERROR S=35 (OPEN INPUT FS) / D2-EXCEPTION-INPUT M=35, M=35 N=35 (OPEN INPUT FM FN) / D3-ERROR-IO twice (OPEN I-O FM FN) / D1-ERROR R=23, X=23 (random READs) / AFTER R=23 X=23
probes.expected: ERROR ON file-names, EXCEPTION ON INPUT and ERROR ON I-O each fire for their files (§1985:VIII.4.8.4 GR5 a, b, d); explicit file-name takes precedence over INPUT (GR4)

probes.expected: USE ... ERROR ON F1 plus USE ... EXCEPTION ON F1 is the same file-name in two USE AFTER EXCEPTION statements: refused (§1985:VIII.4.8.3 SR3 read with SR4)

probes.printed: error COBOL0897: declarative section 'DB': this open mode already has a USE procedure
probes.expected: ERROR ON INPUT plus EXCEPTION ON INPUT is INPUT twice: refused (SR6 read with SR4)

probes.expected: PROCEDURE is underlined in the 1985 format (§1985:VIII.4.8.2), so its omission is refused at 85

probes.printed: error COBOL0878: exception-name EC-I-O was introduced by ISO/IEC 1989:2002; error COBOL0877: USE AFTER EXCEPTION CONDITION requires COBOL-2002
probes.expected: the 2002 Format 3 is not in the 1985 USE format: refused

citations.check: OK  §1985:VIII.4.8.3 SR4  (4.8.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR4

reader.notes: The synonymy is structural: the grammar alternative (EXCEPTION | ERROR) carries no label and DeclBindUse reads only GLOBAL, the operand and its mode, so both spellings bind to the same DeclScope and share the SR3/SR6 registries (_useFiles, _useModes). Probes show each spelling dispatching and the two spellings colliding as duplicates.

refuter.evidence: Attacked the synonymy where the word is consulted indirectly: the 1985 rules that require INVALID KEY / AT END 'if no applicable USE AFTER STANDARD EXCEPTION procedure' (§1985:VIII.4.7.3 SR3 etc.) must be satisfied by an ERROR spelling. r3err-001 (USE AFTER STANDARD ERROR on OUTPUT, INPUT, I-O, EXTEND; WRITE, START, READ, DELETE, REWRITE on relative dynamic and sequential files with no INVALID KEY) compiled and printed DO 22 / DI 23 / DI 23 / DIO 23 / DIO 23 / END; r3exc-001 (same with EXCEPTION) printed identical output. Class c (the IPC-module GLOBAL form §1985:X.5.5.2): r3glob-001 (USE GLOBAL ... ERROR ON INPUT in container, failed OPEN in contained program) and r3glox-001 (EXCEPTION) both print OUTER-GLOBAL 35 / INNER 35 / BACK. r5glob2-001: USE GLOBAL ERROR ON INPUT plus USE EXCEPTION ON INPUT in one Procedure Division refused COBOL0897, so the spellings also collide across GLOBAL. cite.py: OK §1985:VIII.4.8.3 SR4; OK §1985:VIII.4.7.3 SR3.
